title: Observation: int-literal digit separators dropped (thermite-syntax lexer u128); REQ-3 'underscores preserved verbatim' unmet but numerically faithful

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: Source: thermite-syntax lex_int strips '_' and accumulates into Token::Int(u128); AST Expr::IntLit(u128) (ast.rs) carries no raw text, so thermite-lower cannot reproduce separators. Numerically 1000000 == 1_000_000 — NO contract weakening, verus verifies (R-DEFER-9 satisfied). Diverges only from REQ-3's cosmetic parenthetical 'underscores preserved verbatim'; AMENDED REQ-8/AC verify emitted output (passes) and require contract equivalence (holds). Owner: thermite-syntax (representation), not thermite-lower. Low priority per goal.md S8. No failing test filed: there is no soundness divergence to pin (R-CHAR-3 — would be a tautological/cosmetic assertion).

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: [action] Loop 4: L3 lowering SHIPPED (lower.rs + combinator Verus forms); both corpus programs verify in real verus via general shape-keyed templates (critic-proved general). #4 still open: L1 (l1.rs) + effects (effects.rs) remain. main at cc8214c, unpushed.

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: Reshape TokKind::Int and Expr::IntLit to struct variants { value: u128, raw: String } per amended .design/syntax/lexer.md REQ-3 + ast.md REQ-6. lex_int captures source[i..last_digit] as verbatim raw alongside the _-stripped value. Thread { value, raw } / { value, .. } through the full IntLit ripple (parser, lower, l1, effects, validator, mutation, strengthen, vacuity, closure, review). INVARIANT: every emit/lowering/mutation path reads value exactly as the old u128; lower.rs/l1.rs emit value.to_string() so tests/golden/* stay byte-identical (no golden churn). raw is AST-fidelity only; mutated literals set raw=value.to_string(). New round-trip tests assert BOTH fields. Manifest-bounded; critic re-audits.

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: SHIPPED — int literals preserve verbatim raw at the EXPRESSION level (user-chosen enhancement).
